$comment: How AgentCake sorts and judges sessions, in one place. 'verdicts' is the first level, one per session (the API's verdict and the session list's filters); 'unsure' names a stretch the behavior model could not tell (bars, timelines, layers: never a verdict); 'evidence' marks a Human session AgentCake could not tell (no Unknown: such a session counts as human, marked); 'turns' splits an Agent session into Agent only and Human + agent (cake's classes agent and mixed); 'names' says which agent: how sure a product's or an automation tool's name is, or Unnamed when no name fits, shown beside the name (the kind of agent, the verdict's Agent row, and where it runs are reasons, never a category: agentcake/detect/attribute.py; there are no kinds of agent). The dashboard's categories block lists the verdicts with the split inside Agent, and only those; 'counted' says, under it, which visits get a session at all, one paragraph per item ({name} is the product's name, from product.json). The local pages read these labels and sentences when they are built (web/vite.config.ts), the API's words (titles, the coverage note) when it answers. 'classes' says how each class of agentcake/detect/verdict.py is decided, as the session page's summary says it when no single reason decides; Interface text: English only; visitors are Human or Agent, never person, people or user.
title: Reference
counted: {name} only counts visits that run the page script, so crawlers and bots that don't run JavaScript aren't recorded.
AI training crawlers, such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot, and Bytespider, download only the HTML and don't run the page script.
Googlebot's first visit downloads only the HTML and isn't recorded. When Google later renders the page and runs the page script, {name} records it as a Script bot session.

human.label: Human
human.about: Sessions where only a human acted. Sessions that can't be classified are also counted here, with the Limited evidence tag.

agent.label: Agent
agent.about: An AI agent or automation acted in the session, either from start to finish or taking turns with a human.

bot.label: Script bot
bot.about: The visitor is a program on the bot list that ran the page script, such as a search engine or a monitor. Script bot sessions are included in counts but excluded from agent charts.

unsure.label: Unknown
unsure.about: The behavior model couldn't classify the actions in this part of the session. This part isn't counted in the session's classification.

thin.label: Limited evidence
thin.about: This session is counted as Human, but the evidence is limited. For example, it has too few actions, comes from a phone or tablet that can't be confirmed, or has conflicting signals. Its reasons show which one applies.

agent_only.label: Agent only
agent_only.about: An agent acted from start to finish.

human_agent.label: Human + agent
human_agent.about: A human and an agent took turns during the session, and each hand-off appears on the timeline.

verified.label: Verified
verified.about: A signature or a published IP address range confirms the name.

likely.label: Likely
likely.about: The visitor reports this name, or the product leaves its own traces on the page.

unnamed.label: Unnamed
unnamed.about: No product or tool name matches the evidence. The session's reasons list what was detected.

human.how: {name} finds no automation traces or agent names. The behavior model also classifies the actions as human.

agent_ai.how: {name} detects signs of an agent in the page or browser, such as an extension that acts on the page. {name} also detects the fixed setup of cloud computers, and the behavior model classifies the actions as an agent's. The name is based on a verified signature, the product's traces, or the User-Agent.

agent_automated.how: The browser shows automation markers, such as webdriver, a headless browser, or a missing language header. The behavior model splits the session into segments. Crawler-like patterns appear in the reasons as information only.

bot.how: If the User-Agent or a signature matches a program on the bot list, the session isn't analyzed by the behavior model. A published IP address range or a signature marks it “Verified”.

mixed.how: The behavior model finds both a human and an agent in the same session and marks the hand-off where the actions change.

too_little_data.how: The behavior model makes no prediction for phone or tablet visits, or for sessions with too few actions.

not_sure.how: The evidence is too weak or conflicting to classify. For example, traces from open developer tools or keyboard navigation from an assistive tool can look similar.

excluded.how: A page that the browser loaded in advance but never displayed (a prefetch or prerender)
